daysW6.title: El Acebo de San Miguel-> Ponferrada
daysW6.short_desc: Cozy Stays, Global Company and a Quiet City.
daysW6.long_desc: In El Acebo, we stayed in a charming little house run as a bed & breakfast by a kind Dutch couple. The evening before, we had dinner at the hotel located at the bottom of the village, a tasty pilgrim menu that ended on a sweet note with strawberries and cream. Dinner was made even better by the company, Olivia and Robert from Singapore, Julio from Guatemala, and a Frenchman from Paris. The Camino is always full of unexpected, warm conversations from all corners of the world. On Monday, we made the full day walk to Ponferrada. It was a quiet day, as many places were closed due to the National Day holiday, the day before. In the evening, we enjoyed a delicious Italian meal at La Mafia restaurant and checked in to the comfortable Hotel Aroi Ponferrada, which offered a pleasant and restful stay after a long day on the trail.

daysW6.title: Ponferrada -> Villafranca del Bierzo
daysW6.short_desc: Gentle shortcut and a taste of luxury
daysW6.long_desc: After a delicious breakfast, we spent the morning strolling through the streets of Ponferrada, soaking in the charm of the city. Over dinner the night before and again at breakfast, we had the pleasure of chatting with Nancy and Dave, a lovely couple from Fort Lauderdale, Florida, who are walking the Camino for 10 days before heading home via a 14 days cruise. To save Roy’s back and give our legs a break, we opted for a short taxi ride to the nearby village of Cacabelos, just outside Ponferrada. From there, we continued on foot through beautiful vineyards under a clear sky. By afternoon, the temperature hit 25°C and we were both hot, tired, and more than ready for food and rest. We arrived at our destination, Villafranca del Bierzo, where we checked into the Parador Hotel a very welcome touch of comfort on the Camino. The hotel has both an indoor and outdoor pool, although only the indoor one was open. We were reminded of a lovely conversation we had back in Atapuerca with an American diplomat’s wife from Kingston, Jamaica, who had also sung the praises of the Parador hotels. It seems we share a taste for their peaceful charm. The day ended with a delicious dinner at the hotel, a perfect way to wrap up another memorable step on our journey.

daysW6.title: Villafranca del Bierzo -> Vega de Valcarce
daysW6.short_desc: Change of plans, a lucky room, and lobster paella
daysW6.long_desc: We left our beautiful Parador hotel at dawn and began our walk toward Vega de Valcarce, a small village with about 700 inhabitants. We had pre-booked a room that turned out to be part of a bed and breakfast situated directly under a newly built highway, not the most inviting location. The house itself didn’t look very appealing either. So, we decided to continue walking into the village, where we spotted a charming house offering rooms for rent. We asked the hostess if we could see one, and she gladly showed us a lovely, bright room and for only 55 euros. A quick decision was made. Then we remembered that Jackotrans had already delivered our bag to the original accommodation. Roy walked back and retrieved it with a vague excuse, saying we had changed our plans. Meanwhile, our new hostess kindly contacted the logistics company to update the booking so that our bag would be delivered correctly for the next stop. She also told us that the only place in town serving dinner was a small restaurant called Arrocería Español, which opened at 18:00 and closed at 19:00 sharp. We made it there just in time and enjoyed an amazing lobster paella. We chatted with the owner, who shared that it’s tough running a restaurant in such a small village. They’re considering moving their business to O Cebreiro instead. Another unexpected day on the Camino, full of detours, helpful people, and delicious food.

daysW6.title: Vega de Valcarce -> Fonfria
daysW6.short_desc: A taxi ride, mountain views and a modern surprise in Fonfría
daysW6.long_desc: .   Before starting today's walk, our helpful hostess arranged a taxi to take us partway up the mountain to the small village of Laguna de Castilla. This helped shorten the long stage ahead, especially important due to Roy’s back pain. The hike up to O Cebreiro was absolutely beautiful with breathtaking landscapes and fresh mountain air. Once there, we enjoyed a well deserved coffee break in the charming and historic village. Then we began the descent, but first made a short detour to the highest point of the stage. There, we found a small bar where we had some pizza. Unexpectedly, we ran into the Frenchman we had shared dinner with in El Acebo a very fun reunion! We eventually arrived in Fonfría, where we had booked a place that turned out to be a brand-new, modern hostel with eight double rooms clean, fresh, and very comfortable. Dinner was a classic pilgrim’s menu with vegetable soup, a meat dish with fries, and almond cake for dessert. We shared the table with a Dutch pilgrim, a couple from Vienna, and a man from Germany, a lovely and lively group that made for a memorable evening.
